 .....RESPONDENT (BY SHRI RAJIV UPADHYAY - PUBLIC PROSECUTOR)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER
This is the first application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 23.05.2022 by Police Station - Indergarh, District Datia (M.P.) in connection with Crime No.107/2022 registered in relation to the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376-B,
323, 342, 201 of IPC and Section 3/4, 5/6 and 17 of POCSO Act.
As per prosecution story, family of the prosecutrix is well known to the family of the accused persons Ashish, Daulat and Dasrath.

It is alleged that while the prosecutrix had gone to Anganbadi Kendra to collect her meals and was coming back, as the Kendra was closed, on the way of Dabra-Indergarh,
she was forced to sit inside a white Bolero car and she was administered some eatable resulting into her unconsciousness.
When she woke up, she found herself in Gujarat.
The alleged incident is of 28/03/2022.
She has been recovered on 19/05/2022 at Gwalior Railway Station.
Accordingly, the case has been registered.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, her statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. were recorded.

In her statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C she has alleged against accused Mahesh and present applicant, who after kidnapping had taken her to Gujarat where she was kept for one and half months and subjected to sexual abuse by both of them.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that there are material contradictions in the statement of the prosecutrix as the prosecutrix did not mention the name of co-accused Dashrath and Daulat in the statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC, but in her statement under Section 164 of CrPC she also included their names with the allegation that they had beaten her while she was sitting in Bolero car and again in the court statement recorded on 12/10/2022 she has not mentioned the name of the Dashrath and Daulath, such conduct of the prosecutrix goes to show that the present applicant has been falsely implicated.

As a matter of fact, there are differences between the families of the accused and prosecutrix as the house sold to the accused long ago was sought to be taken back from him owing to rise of prices of the house.
The assertion in that behalf was given by the mother of the prosecutrix (P.W.2) in para 4 of her statement, therefore, it is a case of false implication.
It is submitted that charge sheet has been filed, therefore, no custodial interrogation is required.

Furthermore, co-accused Daulat and Dashrath have already been extended the benefit of bail vide order dated 20.02.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.6036 of 2023 and 13.03.2023 in M.Cr.C. No. 9723 of 2023,
respectively.
The applicant is in custody since 23.05.2022.
Conclusion of Trial is likely to take time.
Under such circumstances, applicant may be given the benefit of bail.

Per contra, Shri Upadhyay, learned Panel Lawyer for the State, opposes the application supporting the impugned order with the submission that from the facts of the case complicity of the applicant can not be ruled out.

U p o n hearing learned counsel for the rival parties but without commenting upon the rival contentions touching merits of the case, regard being had to the fact that the applicant is in custody since 23.5.2022, not required for custodial investigation as challan has been filed, co-accused Daulat and Dashrath have since been extended the benefit of bail , hence, the present applicant is held entitled for enlargement on bail.
Consequently, the application of the applicant filed under Section 439 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 is hereby allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court and on the condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and also comply with the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 with following further conditions:
(i) the applicant shall mark his attendance before the concerned police station on second and fourth Saturday every month between 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon.
( ii )
on violation of conditions, State is free to apply for cancellation of bail.
